name: setitimer
synopsis: int setitimer(int which, const struct itimerval *restrict new_value, struct itimerval *_Nullable restrict old_value);
description: The setitimer() system call sets the value of an interval timer for the calling process. It specifies the initial expiration time and optional interval for periodic expiration, after which a signal is generated.

parameters.name: which
parameters.description: Specifies the type of timer (ITIMER_REAL, ITIMER_VIRTUAL, or ITIMER_PROF)

parameters.name: new_value
parameters.description: Pointer to the structure containing the new timer value, including initial value and interval

parameters.name: old_value
parameters.description: Pointer to a structure where the previous timer value will be stored, or NULL if not needed

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: new_value or old_value is not a valid pointer
which is not one of ITIMER_REAL, ITIMER_VIRTUAL, or ITIMER_PROF; or a tv_usec field in new_value is outside the range [0, 999999]

bugs: Under heavy loading, an ITIMER_REAL timer may expire before the previous signal is delivered, leading to lost signals. Before Linux 2.6.16, timer values exceeding a certain limit were silently truncated.
versions: Available since 4.2BSD, POSIX.1-2001, but marked obsolete in POSIX.1-2008
